cards.title: Boolean dimension of posets with planar cover graphs
cards.formal:
Does there exist an integer \(d\ge1\) such that, for every finite poset \(P=(V,<_{P})\) whose undirected cover graph is planar, there exist strict total orders \(L_1,\ldots,L_d\) on \(V\) and a Boolean function \(\varphi_P:\{0,1\}^{d}\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying
\[
\forall x,y\in V\ (x\ne y\Longrightarrow
\bigl[x<_{P}y\iff
\varphi_P(b_1(x,y),\ldots,b_d(x,y))=1\bigr]),
\]
where \(b_i(x,y)=1\) if \(x<_{L_i}y\), and \(b_i(x,y)=0\) otherwise? The integer \(d\) must be independent of the poset. The total orders and the Boolean function may depend on \(P\).
cards.definitions:
A finite poset consists of a finite set \(V\) and an irreflexive, transitive relation \(<_P\). An element \(y\) covers \(x\) if \(x<_P y\) and no \(z\in V\) satisfies \(x<_P z<_P y\). The undirected cover graph is the simple graph with vertex set \(V\) and one edge \(\{x,y\}\) for each such cover relation, with the direction forgotten. It is planar if its vertices can be assigned distinct points of the plane and its edges drawn as simple curves between their endpoints so that edge interiors are disjoint from every vertex and two edge curves meet only at a shared endpoint. The drawing need not place greater elements above smaller ones or make cover edges increase vertically. Planarity of the undirected cover graph, rather than the existence of an upward planar order diagram, is the required hypothesis.

A strict total order \(<_L\) is an irreflexive, transitive relation that, for every two distinct elements, contains exactly one of \(x<_L y\) and \(y<_L x\). Each \(L_i\) orders all of \(V\). The orders may repeat and are auxiliary encodings: they are not required to extend \(<_P\). A Boolean function here is an arbitrary map on the finite set of \(d\)-bit strings; no restriction on its formula size or method of computation is imposed. A sequence of orders and a function satisfying the displayed equivalence is a Boolean realizer of size \(d\). Boolean dimension measures the smallest size of such a realizer; the present question asks only whether these sizes have a universal finite bound.

For each fixed \(P\), the same function \(\varphi_P\) must work for every ordered pair of distinct elements. It cannot depend additionally on the queried pair. An incomparable pair must produce output zero in both orders of its two elements. The equality case is excluded from the equivalence; for empty or one-element ground sets the pair requirement is vacuous. The universal bound applies without restrictions on the number of elements, the size of the largest chain, or the number of minimal or maximal elements. In particular, the poset is not assumed to have a least element. This is an existential structural question with no algorithmic, input-encoding, running-time or randomness requirement.
cards.answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the displayed proposition, including a universal finite bound and the existence of the required realizers for every permitted poset, or a complete Lean proof of its logical negation. The negation means that for every integer \(d\ge1\) there exists a finite poset with a planar undirected cover graph admitting no Boolean realizer of size at most \(d\). A bound depending on the poset size, height or another unbounded parameter, or a bound only for posets with a least element or an upward planar diagram, does not establish the universal positive statement. A conditional result alone does not settle the unconditional target.
cards.why: This asks whether planar local cover relations force a uniformly bounded comparison description of the entire partial order, despite arbitrarily large ordinary order dimension. A positive answer would also give logarithmic-size reachability labels for planar directed graphs, connecting a structural question about orders with concise representations of global reachability.

importance.reason: A constant-size Boolean description of every order with a planar cover graph would explain how planar local structure controls global order information.

progress.text: Nešetřil and Pudlák pose bounded Boolean dimension for posets with planar order diagrams; the broader cover-graph formulation is distinguished explicitly in later primary sources.
Revision 2 retains Problem A for arbitrary planar cover graphs and proves the bound \(13\) with a unique minimal element.
Revision 2 of Boolean Dimension of a Boolean Lattice explicitly describes planar-cover-graph boundedness as an open problem.
Revision 3 of Cliquewidth and Dimension gives bounded Boolean dimension for bounded cliquewidth and continues to state the unrestricted planar-cover-graph question as open.
Cliquewidth and Dimension is first published in Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, volume 132, issue 1, article e70116.

context_blocks.text: Problem A explicitly asks this question for planar undirected cover graphs. Its footnote records that the question originally posed by Nešetřil and Pudlák in 1989 concerned the more restricted class admitting planar order diagrams. This card retains the broader formulation stated in the later primary papers; it does not attribute the two scopes as identical.

Blake, Micek and Trotter prove \(\operatorname{bdim}(P)\le13\) when the cover graph is planar and \(P\) has a unique minimal element. In a finite nonempty poset, this is a least element, meaning an element below every other element. The additional hypothesis is absent from the general question.

Ordinary order dimension requires total orders that extend the partial order and reconstruct it by taking their intersection. Boolean realizers allow arbitrary auxiliary total orders and an arbitrary Boolean decoder. The known examples of large ordinary dimension with planar cover graphs do not automatically have large Boolean dimension.

Joret, Micek, Pilipczuk and Walczak prove bounded Boolean dimension for posets of bounded cliquewidth. This parameter concerns construction of the full directed order relation using a bounded set of vertex labels and uniform operations on label classes; it is not a hypothesis supplied merely by planarity of the cover graph. Their October 2025 revision explicitly retains the planar-cover-graph question as open.

The reachability connection concerns labels assigned to vertices of a directed graph, from which one fixed decoder decides whether a directed path joins the two queried vertices. Bounded Boolean dimension for all posets in this question would imply labels of \(O(\log n)\) bits for planar directed graphs with \(n\) vertices. This is a consequence motivating the target, not an additional required theorem.

The March 2025 revision of Boolean Dimension of a Boolean Lattice independently lists planar-cover-graph boundedness as open. Its results about inclusion orders on subsets do not settle this planar question.

sentences: The cover graph records which pairs in a finite partial order are immediately comparable, with edge directions forgotten.
The question asks whether planarity of that graph guarantees a universal constant number of total orders encoding every comparability.
One Boolean function decodes the comparison bits for all distinct ordered pairs, and both that function and the auxiliary orders may vary with the poset.
The orders need not extend the partial order, and no upward planar diagram or unique minimal element is assumed.
Known bounds with additional structural hypotheses leave the general question open in the checked sources and motivate its connection to concise reachability labels.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
